newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Sao Paulo state debt accord expected on Thursday.
newsitem.headline: Sao Paulo state debt accord expected on Thursday.

text.p: Brazil's federal government is likely to sign a final debt-restructuring agreement with Sao Paulo state on Thursday, a Finance Ministry official said on Wednesday.
Pedro Parente, executive secretary of the ministry, told reporters that one or two issues still had to be settled, but it was likely a final accord would be signed Thursday.

"On the federal government's side, everything is ready for the accord. We think it is possible to sign the agreement tomorrow," Parente said, adding that 13 contracts are to be signed under the accord.

Late last year, Sao Paulo and the federal government agreed to refinance the state's debt under a broader restructuring program. Under the deal, Sao Paulo state bank control for one year and prepared for its privatization.
Sao Paulo's debt now totals 50 billion reais, of which 20 billion reais is owed to Banespa.

Banespa shares have surged in the past few sessions amid expectations that a Sao Paulo debt accord was imminent. Trading in the bank's shares was halted on Wednesday after a newspaper reported that an agreement would be announced Thursday.
